jobs.title: Senior Sourcing Specialist or Lead Sourcing Specialist
jobs.description:
Important Application Submission Information
In order to ensure your application is successfully received before the job posting expires, please submit your application by 11:59 PM on Tuesday, October 20, 2026
More than a career - a chance to make a difference in people's lives.

Build an exciting, rewarding career with us – help us make a difference for millions of people every day. Consider joining the Duke Energy team, where you'll find a friendly work environment, opportunities for growth and development, recognition for your work, and competitive pay and benefits.

Depending upon the desired qualifications of the successful applicant, the hiring manager may elect to fill this position at a higher level within the job hierarchy.

Relocation assistance is being offered for this position.

Position Summary
This Senior Sourcing Specialist position is the third level of the Nuclear Sourcing classification hierarchy and is responsible for developing and executing strategic sourcing plans in support of evaluating potential new nuclear generation. This role provides an opportunity for an experienced sourcing professional to lead complex, high-value procurement activities supporting one of Duke Energy’s most significant potential capital investment programs. The position supports sourcing of materials, equipment, long-lead items, engineering, construction, fabrication, testing, logistics, warehousing, and professional services required to evaluate and potentially develop new nuclear generation.

The Senior Sourcing Specialist will lead the full strategic sourcing lifecycle, including opportunity assessment, demand and category analysis, supply-market assessment, sourcing strategy development, competitive bid events, supplier evaluations, negotiations, contract development, supplier readiness, and performance management. The position will manage complex and high-value sourcing initiatives where commercial strategy, supplier capability, schedule, quality, and risk management are critical to project success.

A successful candidate will bring strong strategic sourcing and negotiation experience, commercial judgment, analytical capability, and the ability to influence stakeholders across a complex enterprise. The individual will work proactively with the Nuclear Business Unit, Project Management & Construction (PMC), Nuclear Operations, Engineering, Project Controls, Legal, Finance, Treasury/Tax, Cybersecurity, Credit Risk, Insurance, Quality/Nuclear Oversight, and supplier stakeholders to develop practical sourcing solutions and build alignment across organizations.

The ideal candidate is a proactive sourcing professional who can translate technical and project requirements into effective commercial strategies, challenge assumptions, identify opportunities, manage supplier and commercial risk, and communicate recommendations clearly to project and executive leadership. Employees at this level are fully competent in applicable sourcing concepts and procedures, work independently on most assignments, identify problems, develop solutions, and escalate unusual or complex issues appropriately.

Responsibilities
- Sourcing Strategy Development: Develop and present sourcing strategies for complex, high-value materials, equipment, engineering, construction, fabrication, testing, transportation, warehousing, and professional services. Evaluate competitive sourcing options, market conditions, supplier capabilities, project requirements, commercial alternatives, and risk to recommend sourcing approaches that support project schedule, quality, cost, and enterprise objectives.
- Strategy Execution and Governance: Lead end-to-end sourcing activities including RFIs, RFPs, competitive bid events, supplier evaluations, commercial evaluations, award recommendations, governance reviews, contract releases, purchase order releases, and supplier onboarding. Establish clear evaluation criteria, document sourcing decisions, coordinate required approvals, and ensure effective handoffs to contract management, supplier performance management, project controls, and execution teams.
- Negotiation and Commercial Value Delivery: Develop negotiation strategies and lead commercial negotiations with supplier management for high-value and complex contracts. Negotiate pricing, escalation, payment terms, schedule commitments, milestones, warranties, remedies, change management, intellectual property, confidentiality, audit rights, flow-down requirements, and other commercial provisions. Use should-cost models, market intelligence, commodity and escalation indices, historical benchmarks, competitive analysis, and total-cost-of-ownership approaches to support fact-based negotiations and deliver measurable commercial value.
- Risk, Compliance and Quality Requirements: Proactively identify and manage sourcing and supplier risks that could affect cost, schedule, quality, project execution, or regulatory compliance. Partner with Legal, Tax/Treasury, Credit Risk, Insurance, Cybersecurity, Engineering, Nuclear Oversight/Quality, and other subject matter experts to evaluate and address technical, contractual, financial, cybersecurity, domestic content, FEOC, IRA, prevailing wage/apprenticeship, logistics, quality, regulatory, and supplier capacity risks.
- Supplier Qualification, Performance, and Corrective Action: Lead commercial and supply-chain assessments of suppliers and sub-suppliers, including evaluation of capability, quality programs, delivery performance, financial stability, capacity, workforce readiness, manufacturing capability, supply-chain resiliency, geopolitical exposure, documentation/traceability, and ability to support project milestones. Monitor supplier commitments and performance, support corrective actions, resolve escalated commercial issues, and communicate supplier risks through appropriate metrics and governance forums.
- Business Partner, Project, and Stakeholder Management: Serve as a strategic supply chain partner to Nuclear Business Unit, Project Management & Construction (PMC), Nuclear Operations, Engineering, Project Controls, Legal, Finance, Tax, and project execution teams. Build strong internal and supplier relationships, translate technical and project requirements into effective sourcing strategies, facilitate cross-functional decision making, and develop solutions that balance technical, commercial, schedule, quality, and risk objectives.
- Change Management and Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve sourcing processes, supplier engagement, project visibility, governance, and execution. Support implementation plans, lessons learned, digital reporting, sourcing metrics, supplier readiness reviews, templates, and tools that strengthen sourcing effectiveness and support consistent execution across potential new nuclear projects.
- Leadership and Knowledge Sharing: Provide cross-training, coaching, and guidance to sourcing personnel and business partners. Share sourcing best practices and develop practical job aids, sourcing templates, supplier evaluation criteria, negotiation strategies, and procedural guidance. Contribute to the continued development of New Nuclear Generation sourcing capabilities and a strong culture of commercial discipline, collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Required/Basic Qualifications
Senior Sourcing Specialist
- Bachelor's degree
- 5 years related work experience

- In lieu of Bachelor's degree(s) AND 5 year(s) related work experience listed above, Associates degree AND 7 year(s) or High School/GED AND 9 year(s) related work experience

Lead Sourcing Specialist
- Bachelor's degree
- 7 years related work experience

- In lieu of Bachelor's degree(s) AND 7 year(s) related work experience listed above, Associates degree AND 9 year(s) or High School/GED AND 11 year(s) related work experience

Preferred Qualifications
- Graduate degree in Supply Chain, Business, Engineering, Finance, Construction Management, Project Management, or related field.
- C.P.M. (Certified Purchasing Manager), CPSM (Certified Professional in Supply Management), CSCP (Certified Supply Chain Professional), CPIM (Certified in Production and Inventory Management), PMP (Project Management Professional), or similar sourcing, supply chain, project management, or technical certification.
- Demonstrated experience leading strategic sourcing initiatives, competitive sourcing events, supplier proposal evaluations, commercial negotiations, contract development, and supplier performance activities for complex or high-value categories.
- Experience sourcing equipment, materials, engineering, construction, fabrication, logistics, or professional services supporting utilities, energy, infrastructure, manufacturing, industrial facilities, major capital projects, or other technically complex environments.
- Demonstrated ability to develop category and sourcing strategies, analyze supply markets, identify qualified suppliers, create supplier evaluation criteria, conduct commercial evaluations, and develop executive-ready sourcing recommendations.
- Strong commercial and financial acumen, including experience with pricing analysis, total-cost-of-ownership analysis, benchmarking, escalation indices, should-cost approaches, payment structures, and commercial risk evaluation.
- Experience negotiating high-value or complex contracts involving pricing, escalation, schedule commitments, milestones, warranties, remedies, change management, audit rights, intellectual property, and risk allocation.
- Strong supplier relationship and performance management experience, including supplier qualification, capability assessments, performance reviews, issue resolution, corrective actions, capacity evaluations, and supply-chain risk mitigation.
- Demonstrated ability to work effectively with cross-functional teams including engineering, project management, construction, legal, finance, quality, operations, and executive leadership.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with demonstrated ability to develop clear business cases, sourcing recommendations, negotiation strategies, risk assessments, presentations, and executive-level communications.
- Experience supporting major capital projects, power generation, utilities, nuclear, manufacturing, industrial construction, EPC projects, long-lead equipment procurement, modular construction, or technically complex supply chains.
- Knowledge of supplier risk considerations including financial health, capacity, quality, cybersecurity, insurance, logistics, regulatory compliance, domestic content, and supply-chain resiliency.
- Working knowledge of nuclear procurement and quality requirements for safety-related and non-safety-related materials, equipment, and services, including NRC, NUPIC, ASME NQA-1, 10 CFR Part 21, and 10 CFR Part 50 Appendix B concepts.
- Experience supporting supplier readiness assessments, manufacturing or fabrication facility evaluations, source inspections, supplier development, or major equipment procurement.
- Completion of the EPRI Nuclear Utility Procurement Course or comparable nuclear procurement/quality training.
- Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook/Teams, CoPilot AI, and applicable procurement, contract management, ERP, sourcing, document management, and reporting tools.

Working Conditions
- Hybrid Mobility Classification – Work will be performed from both remote and onsite locations after the onboarding period. However, hybrid employees must live within a reasonable commute to their designated Duke Energy facility, not greater than 50 miles one way. Employees are expected to report to their assigned Duke Energy facility as required and directed by their manager, on average 3 full workdays per regular workweek.
- Office setting
- Periodic meetings at Duke Energy facilities, project sites, supplier locations, fabrication/manufacturing facilities, and industry conferences.

- 25-50% travel, primarily domestic with opportunities for international travel, offers the chance to work directly with leading suppliers and engage firsthand with the nuclear manufacturing and project supply chain. Travel may include supplier and fabrication facility visits, project sites, strategic negotiations, readiness assessments, source inspections, logistics planning, and industry events supporting the development of new nuclear generation.

- Work may involve time-sensitive sourcing decisions, supplier escalations, negotiations, project requirements, executive review materials, and coordination across multiple internal and external stakeholders.

Specific Requirements
- Bachelor's degree + 5 years work experience OR
- Associate's degree + 7 years work experience OR
- HS/GED + 9 years work experience
- Must possess, or obtain within 3 months of start, Position Specific Guide qualifications for both materials and services sourcing: NSCD-285A Nuclear Sourcing Purchase Order PSG and NSCD-284B Nuclear Sourcing Contract PSG.

Turbine and Generator Services (TGS) exists to provide programmatic engineering and technical support to the Regulated and Renewable Energy (RRE) fleet of turbines and generators.  We embrace and diligently pursue the vision of zero major events for these centerline assets resulting in substantial and sustained improvements in station availability/reliability and exceptional long-term shareholder value.  TGS is committed to relentlessly and purposefully leveraging people, organizations, information, technology, and analytical techniques to identify, evaluate and address any issue that could contribute to a major event.

This position will be responsible for managing Long Term Service Agreements with major Turbine/Generator OEMs.

This position is the expert level of the Generation Program Manager hierarchy and is responsible for the development and implementation of comprehensive programmatic strategies for the RRE fleet of turbines and generators.  These strategies address corporate strategic objectives, financial goals, regulatory requirements, technology limitations, and OEM/vendor relationships.  The Program Manager will ensure adequate and consistent plans, processes, documentation, and standards are developed, trained, implemented, and exercised to ensure all RRE sites maintain compliance with the program outline.  At this level, the employee will solve the most complex problems and will have wide latitude for unreviewed work and proposals submitted to Senior Leadership teams.  Assignments at this level require the highest level of critical thinking to resolve high-impact, complex and/or cross-functional problems.  Incumbents are expected to have advanced skills, work independently and are to be considered industry experts in their discipline or in a particular field.  They consult on strategic and highly complex work.

The incumbent must have leadership ability, organizational knowledge, experience, and strategic vision to implement relevant programs to address issues in the fleet. The incumbent must possess the technical acumen to design/analyze/assess program details, have proficiency in financial or economic analysis to optimize results and recommend adjustment to program initiatives, all to achieve defined improvement results.

The position requires excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to lead the preparation of complex reports and presentations.  This level will frequently interface with all levels of management including GMs, VPs, Senior VPs, and the senior management groups.

The position requires a high level of coordination skills as well as the ability to manage complex technical projects involving other departments, outside consultants and industry groups.  The Program Manager is expected to frequently interface with industry groups and peers to benchmark best practices and to lead the industry in a rapidly changing environment.

Responsibilities:

- Continually evaluate changing and emergent fleet events, industry developments, supplier changes, environmental legislation, regulatory drivers, and corporate strategic direction to identify opportunities to improve the performance and cost effectiveness of program strategies.  Prepare reports, white papers, and/or presentations which address technically complex and financially significant issues
- Leads the development and scoping of new improvement initiatives across the fleet to maintain compliance with standards and company governance and policies.  Provides technical leadership for the execution of program initiatives. Effectively communicates the results of initiatives to senior management and other stakeholders.  Build consensus through these efforts and secure project approval and funding when appropriate
- Manage existing and develop new business relationships with OEMs and other vendors to ensure our business and other needs are being met (such as safety, quality work, good value, financial needs, warranty, etc.). Identify opportunities for multi-year vendor relationships to leverage cost savings and bundling opportunities. Assist with the resolution of contract performance commercial issues when stalled at the project level.
- Develop and lead routine program assessment activities to provide early identification of gaps and program issues.  Provide support for RRE stations during audits, assessments, and outage preparation and execution activities. Create tools and templates to perform gap analysis on important programmatic areas and prioritize recommendations that will lead to improvement action plans.
- Influence business unit leaders on implementation of consistent standards across the business unit.  Lead industry peer groups to ensure company engagement with emerging issues. Actively integrates industry best practices into Duke Energy fleet initiatives and programs.  Establish metrics and KPIs in support of fleet initiatives and business targets. Revise initiatives to respond to changing industry/fleet trends and priorities

Basic/Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree and 10 years related experience
- In Lieu of Bachelor’s Degree - HS Diploma / GED and 18 years related experience.

Additional Preferred Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s in Engineering/Science/Business, or PE License
- Strong collaboration/interpersonal skills and written/verbal communication skills
- Business acumen and ability to interpret regulatory language

Working Conditions:

- Hybrid Mobility Classification – Work will be performed from both remote and onsite locations after the onboarding period. However, hybrid employees must live within a reasonable commute to their designated Duke Energy facility, not greater than 50 miles one way. Employees are expected to report to their assigned Duke Energy facility as required and directed by their manager, on average 3 full workdays per regular workweek.
- Primary location will be TGS Lark Facility in Mt. Holly/Charlotte area
- Travel 15-20%

Travel Requirements
15-25%

Yes

No

Why Join Supply Chain Innovation & Analytics?
The Supply Chain Innovation & Analytics team identifies opportunities, solves complex business challenges, and drives strategic initiatives that create measurable operational and financial value for Duke Energy.
This role provides direct exposure to senior leaders and enterprise-wide initiatives, offering the opportunity to influence strategy, improve business performance, strengthen governance, and help shape the future of how the company delivers operational and financial results.

Duke Energy is seeking first year Master of Business Administration (MBA) students with a passion for the energy sector!

The Duke Energy MBA Interns will be working on special projects throughout the summer and interfacing with various teams both internal and external to Duke Energy. This role is a temporary internship assignment during the Summer of 2027.  The primary job responsibility will be to assist with the projects and teams related to their assigned business unit.  Internship opportunities will provide meaningful contributions in support of Duke’s clean energy transition strategy, actual project work leading to decision-oriented results, and broad exposure to groups and initiatives within Duke Energy.

You MUST apply to the job posting on the Duke Energy careers page to be considered. A current transcript and resume must be submitted with your application.

Program Locations for 2027: Charlotte, NC; Raleigh, NC

Potential for opportunities at locations across our footprint: North Carolina, South Carolina, Indiana, Ohio, Kentucky, and Florida.

Overview of Duke Energy Hiring Organizations
Potential opportunities for Summer 2027 include the following (these may be updated based upon emerging needs in the business):

- Regulated Renewables Development : Want to be a renewables developer and work towards bringing new utility scale generation projects to the grid? Join the development team responsible for originating, developing, acquiring, and executing utility-scale solar, solar paired with storage and wind projects within Duke Energy’s six regulated service territories. MBA interns will assist in all aspects of project development, including land acquisition, interconnection requests, environmental and technical diligence, permitting, project acquisition due diligence, financial modeling, transaction approvals and project execution.

- Energy Storage Development Team: be a part of exciting efforts as the organization plans efforts to develop and sponsor lithium battery energy storage projects.

- Project Management and Construction: PMC is responsible for building our new power generation assets and is in early stages of the largest buildout in the history of the company.  As part of Duke Energy’s broader strategy to meet rising customer demand and decarbonize the grid, PMC is actively planning and building renewable solar and bulk energy storage, new simple and combined cycle turbines, as well as developing projects for advanced nuclear, pumped storage hydro, and other emerging technologies. MBA interns could include work on project controls and analytics for large renewable, gas, or battery projects in the Carolinas, either transitioning to construction or in construction.

- Finance: MBA interns could be placed in various roles within the Finance organization, including financial planning & analysis budgeting/forecasting, and working closely on financial related matters with other teams within Duke Energy.

- Natural Gas: Internship supporting the expanded natural gas development activities within the company, curated to the individuals interests and team needs.

- Distributed Energy: This team works on aspects of small distributed energy resources including interconnection study, deployment, operations, and maintenance.

- Emerging Technology Office: Enable the adoption of emerging technologies to support the goals of Duke Energy and our customers.

- Enrolled and actively pursuing a Master of Business Administration degree from an accredited college or university with an anticipated graduation of spring/summer 2028.

- Interested in working in Duke Energy service territories.
- Experience directing cross-functional teams.

- Extensive scheduling and planning experience.

- Project Management Professional certification (for PMC role).
